difficulty:0.en: Master Qingwu set eight scrolls on the stone table, each sealed with a different color of light. 'Copy the root-word before the candle burns down,' she said. The first three came easily. The fourth stopped me cold — its strokes kept unraveling like smoke. That single *difficulty* swallowed the whole evening, yet when the word finally held its shape, warmth spread across my palm like sunrise.
difficulty:0.cnHint: 我在抄写第四个根字时遇到了巨大的____，几乎耗尽了整个夜晚。
difficulty:0.hook: Outside, the candle flame bent west — though no wind was blowing.
difficulty:0.line: 'Every *difficulty* you push through becomes a root inside you,' said Master Qingwu.

full:0.en: Shen Wujiu brought a small clay jar to my room and placed it on the windowsill without a word. Inside, tiny golden characters floated in clear liquid — a whole season of gathered herb-words. 'Drink when the moon is *full*,' he said quietly. I counted the characters. There were exactly thirty, one for each night of study ahead.
full:0.cnHint: 师兄带来一罐盛满字灵的药液，叮嘱我在月____时饮下。
full:0.hook: When he left, the jar hummed once — low, like a warning bell.
full:0.line: 'Drink only when the moon is *full*, or the words will scatter,' Shen Wujiu said.

range:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long map across the floor, tracing the floating peaks that formed our sect's territory. 'A disciple's voice must carry across this entire *range* of mountains before the trial ends,' she said. I looked at the distance between the nearest peak and the farthest — a gap wide enough to swallow clouds. My throat felt very small.
range:0.cnHint: 师尊指着地图说，弟子的声音必须传遍整个山____，才算通过考验。
range:0.hook: One peak on the map had no name written beneath it.
range:0.line: 'Your words must reach every mountain in this *range*,' Master Qingwu said.

region:0.en: The inner hall held a glass cabinet filled with scrolls sorted by origin. Each *region* of the cloud sea produced herbs with a different spiritual flavor — bitter from the northern fog, sweet from the eastern light. I was told to choose one scroll and study it before dawn. My hand hovered, then settled on a scroll from an unnamed southern zone, its edges dark with old rain.
region:0.cnHint: 内殿收藏了来自不同____的字草卷轴，我在黎明前必须选定一卷研读。
region:0.hook: The scroll I chose was the only one that felt warm to the touch.
region:0.line: 'Each *region* gives its words a different spirit — choose with care,' said Master Qingwu.

material:0.en: Xiaoxing spread her notes across my desk, pointing to a list of twelve herb-words used in a healing formula. 'The written word is the *material* the formula is built from,' she explained, 'the way stone is the material of a wall.' I had thought only the spoken sound mattered. Seeing the ink lines as building blocks changed something in how I held my brush.
material:0.cnHint: 师妹解释说，书写的字词是构筑法术的____，就如同石头是墙壁的根基。
material:0.hook: One of her notes had a character I did not recognize — and it was moving.
material:0.line: 'Treat each word as *material*, solid and exact,' Xiaoxing told me.

pressure:0.en: The trial required holding a single word-form in my mind while Master Qingwu pressed two fingers lightly to my temple. The *pressure* was not physical — it was like a second voice trying to rewrite the word before I could fix it in place. Three disciples before me had let the form dissolve. I breathed slowly, held the shape, and felt the second voice go still.
pressure:0.cnHint: 师尊以双指轻抵我的额头，那无形的____试图在我心中改写字形。
pressure:0.hook: When she lifted her fingers, my shadow on the wall was facing the wrong way.
pressure:0.line: 'The *pressure* will not stop — your word must be stronger,' Master Qingwu said.

thus:0.en: Each herb-word in the canon was paired with its opposite, and mastering both was the rule. 'A word of fire studied alone will burn the user,' Shen Wujiu explained. 'The old masters always learned in pairs, and *thus* none of them were lost to their own power.' I looked at the fire-word glowing on my page and immediately reached for the water-word beside it.
thus:0.cnHint: 师兄说古代宗师总是成对修习字法，____没有一人被自身的力量所伤。
thus:0.hook: The fire-word flickered twice, as if it had heard us talking about it.
thus:0.line: 'They studied in pairs and *thus* kept themselves whole,' said Shen Wujiu.

tool:0.en: Xiaoxing picked up my brush, turned it slowly, and set it back down. 'A brush is only a *tool*,' she said. 'It does not carry the word — you do.' I had been blaming every crooked stroke on the old brush Master Qingwu had given me. After Xiaoxing spoke, I tried again with the same brush. The stroke came out clean and straight, almost bright.
tool:0.cnHint: 师妹告诉我，笔只是一件____，字的力量来自执笔之人。
tool:0.hook: The clean stroke began to glow faintly before the ink had dried.
tool:0.line: 'A brush is just a *tool* — the word lives in your hand,' Xiaoxing said.

international:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a scroll so old its edges had turned to dust. 'This formula,' she said softly, 'was not born on our mountain alone. Sects from every distant peak contributed one character each, making it *international* in a way no single school could claim.' I traced the joined brushstrokes and felt many minds breathing inside them.
international:0.cnHint: 师尊展示一卷由各方门派共同书写的功法，说明这个词的____属性。
international:0.hook: Yet one character near the centre was written in a hand no living master recognised.
international:0.line: 'This word-formula is *international* — it belongs to every sect under the clouds.'

manage:0.en: The ink-lamp flickered as I tried for the fifth time to hold the healing word 'still' inside my mind without letting it dissolve. Shen Wujiu watched from the doorway. 'You have to *manage* both your breath and your intention at once,' he said, 'or the word escapes like smoke.' On my sixth try, a faint green glow finally held.
manage:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，要同时____好呼吸和心念，才能留住那个疗愈的字。
manage:0.hook: But the lamp cast two shadows where only one person stood.
manage:0.line: 'If you cannot *manage* your breath, the word will never stay.'

outside:0.en: Snow had settled on the inner courtyard tiles, and Xiaoxing pressed her face to the paper window. 'What word lives *outside* the sect's library, in open air?' she asked no one. Master Qingwu, passing with a candle, paused. 'Every word you have not yet needed,' she answered, and walked on without slowing.
outside:0.cnHint: 小星望着窗____，师尊说那里藏着所有你尚未需要的字。
outside:0.hook: A single set of footprints in the snow led away from the library and did not return.
outside:0.line: 'The rarest words grow *outside*, where no roof can shelter them.'

fun:0.en: Shen Wujiu juggled three small word-stones above his palm, making them hum different tones. 'People think cultivation is only suffering,' he said, grinning. 'But there is real *fun* in learning a new word — it feels like catching a firefly that decided to cooperate.' I laughed, and for a moment the coming trial felt very far away.
fun:0.cnHint: 师兄说，学到一个新字其实有真正的____，就像抓住一只愿意配合的萤火虫。
fun:0.hook: Then all three stones turned cold and dark at exactly the same instant.
fun:0.line: 'Find the *fun* in a hard word, or the hard word will never open for you.'

reality:0.en: I had memorised the flight-word perfectly, yet when I stepped to the ledge the mountain felt terrifyingly solid beneath my feet. Master Qingwu stood behind me. 'Your mind knows the word,' she said, 'but the *reality* of empty air is testing whether your body believes it too.' I breathed out, leaned forward, and the clouds received me.
reality:0.cnHint: 师尊说，真正的____是空气的虚空在考验我的身体是否真的相信那个飞行之字。
reality:0.hook: Far below, something large moved through the cloud layer and did not surface.
reality:0.line: 'The *reality* of the drop is the only teacher left now.'

beyond:0.en: Xiaoxing spread her notes across the study mat, each page dense with copied words. 'I have learned everything in the first archive,' she said quietly. Master Qingwu set a second, thicker scroll beside the pile. 'Good. Now begin what lies *beyond* that archive — the words the sect almost forgot.' Xiaoxing's brush hand trembled slightly as she reached for it.
beyond:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉小星，第一册之____还有一卷更厚的，那里记着门派几乎遗忘的字。
beyond:0.hook: The scroll's ribbon was sealed with wax the colour of a dying ember.
beyond:0.line: 'True mastery begins only *beyond* the last page you feel comfortable reading.'

completely:0.en: I woke before dawn to find the word I had been struggling with *completely* clear in my mind, as if the night had dissolved every knot I had tied around it. Shen Wujiu said this sometimes happened — sleep did a kind of invisible weaving. I rose, inked my brush, and wrote it in one stroke without hesitation.
completely:0.cnHint: 一觉醒来，我发现那个令我困扰的字____清晰了，仿佛夜晚化解了所有阻碍。
completely:0.hook: The brushstroke dried in seconds, then began, very faintly, to glow on its own.
completely:0.line: 'Once a word is *completely* yours, it will write itself before you think it.'

advise:0.en: The eve of the trial had arrived. Master Qingwu gathered us around the ink-stone table and spoke without ceremony. 'I *advise* you each to carry only three words tomorrow — one to shield, one to move, one to see clearly.' She tapped the table once. 'More will tangle. Three, held well, are enough.' We nodded, and the candle between us bent without wind.
advise:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师尊____我们明天只带三个字上阵：护体、移身、明心。
advise:0.hook: The candle flame bent sharply toward the door, though every window was shut.
advise:0.line: 'I *advise* you: three words held well outweigh thirty words held loosely.'

describe:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a scroll older than memory. 'Before you may speak a healing word,' she said, 'you must first *describe* it — its colour, its weight, the feeling it leaves on the tongue.' I closed my eyes and tried. The word tasted like rain on warm stone. Around us, the candles burned without smoke.
describe:0.cnHint: 师尊要求弟子用语言____出每个灵字的感觉，才能开始修习治愈之术。
describe:0.hook: Then one candle flame turned, slowly, to face the door.
describe:0.line: '*Describe* the word exactly — its colour, its weight, nothing less.'

rest:0.en: Shen Wujiu found me slumped over the scripture table long past midnight. 'A word held too tightly breaks,' he said softly, setting a cup of warm tea beside my hand. 'Even spiritual fire needs *rest* to burn bright again.' I nodded, too tired to speak. Outside, the cloud sea rose higher than usual.
rest:0.cnHint: 师兄劝我，灵力修炼也需要____，否则反而会适得其反。
rest:0.hook: The clouds outside pressed against the window like a held breath.
rest:0.line: 'Spiritual fire also needs *rest* — push any harder and it will crack.'

employer:0.en: A messenger arrived at the inner hall bearing a sealed letter. The letter named the Sect as *employer* of three wandering word-healers, binding them to our mountain for the coming trial season. Master Qingwu read it twice, then set it face-down on the table without a word.
employer:0.cnHint: 一封信件指明门派是三位游历灵医的____，将他们召来备战。
employer:0.hook: The candle beside her hand went out with no wind to blame.
employer:0.line: 'The Sect stands as *employer* — they are bound to answer our call.'

owner:0.en: Xiaoxing pressed a small jade slip into my palm. 'This word belongs to you now,' she whispered. 'You are its *owner*. Guard it.' I felt the character pulse once, warm and certain, against my skin. No one had ever trusted me with a living word before. Somewhere beneath us, a deep bell rang once.
owner:0.cnHint: 师妹告诉我，那枚玉简中的灵字已经认我为____，要我好好守护它。
owner:0.hook: The bell's echo did not fade — it grew, note by note, into something else.
owner:0.line: 'You are its *owner* now — it will answer no one else until you release it.'

gender:0.en: A senior disciple once told me that the oldest healing words carry no *gender* — they were shaped before the sect divided its robes into colours. Master Qingwu confirmed it quietly: 'A word that heals does not ask who is holding it.' I wrote that down. The ink dried silver instead of black.
gender:0.cnHint: 师尊解释说，最古老的灵字没有____之分，对所有修行者一视同仁。
gender:0.hook: The silver ink slowly formed a shape none of us recognised.
gender:0.line: 'The oldest words have no *gender* — they were made for every hand alike.'

website:0.en: A young outer disciple showed me a glowing spirit-board — a *website* woven from light threads, where disciples across distant peaks shared notes on rare words. I had never seen such a thing. Shen Wujiu leaned over my shoulder, quiet for a long moment. 'Useful,' he said at last. 'And dangerous.'
website:0.cnHint: 一位外门弟子展示了一块灵光织成的____，用来在各山峰之间传递灵字心得。
website:0.hook: One thread of light on the board pulsed red and did not stop.
website:0.line: 'This *website* links every peak — one wrong word and all of them will know.'

emotional:0.en: Before the night trial, Xiaoxing sat very still, hands folded, eyes bright with something she would not name. 'Are you ready?' I asked. 'Being *emotional* does not make me weak,' she said clearly. 'It makes the words I carry heavier — and sharper.' I had nothing to answer. The mountain trembled once, faintly.
emotional:0.cnHint: 师妹说，____并不是软弱，反而让她掌握的灵字更有分量。
emotional:0.hook: The faint trembling moved upward, through our feet, into our chests.
emotional:0.line: 'Being *emotional* does not slow me — it sharpens every word I hold.'

training:0.en: For thirty days our *training* had been this: one word, one hour, total silence. Master Qingwu said nothing could be rushed — not soil, not stone, not a word that wished to live inside you. On the thirty-first morning she arrived early, carrying a scroll none of us had seen. Her expression gave nothing away.
training:0.cnHint: 入门三十天的____只做一件事：每天用一个时辰，在沉默中感受一个灵字。
training:0.hook: The scroll in her arms was sealed with a mark that looked like a closing eye.
training:0.line: 'Your *training* ends at dawn — what you carry now, you carry into the trial.'

consume:0.en: The night before the great trial, Master Qingwu lit seven spirit lamps and placed a bowl of warm broth before me. 'A disciple who lets worry *consume* their strength before dawn will have nothing left to give,' she said softly. I drank every drop and felt the cold fear in my chest slowly loosen.
consume:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师尊告诫我不要让忧虑____掉所有的力气，并亲手为我备了一碗热汤。
consume:0.hook: Outside, the seventh lamp flickered once — then went dark.
consume:0.line: 'Do not let worry *consume* you before the trial even begins.'

desire:0.en: Shen Wujiu sat across from me in the study hall, copying word-formulas by candlelight. He did not look up when he spoke. 'I *desire* nothing this night except to understand the last glyph,' he murmured. His brush moved like a quiet river, certain and unhurried, and I felt my own restless heart grow still.
desire:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师兄在灯下抄写法诀，说他此刻唯一的____是弄懂最后一个字符。
desire:0.hook: Then the candle cast two shadows where only one person sat.
desire:0.line: 'I *desire* only to understand this final glyph before morning comes.'

meal:0.en: Xiaoxing appeared at my door carrying a small wooden tray. She had prepared a simple *meal* of soft rice and pickled root, the kind our first lesson called 'the scholar's supper.' She set it down without ceremony and sat beside me while I ate, her silence warmer than any speech.
meal:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师妹为我送来了一顿简单的____，陪伴着我，一言不发。
meal:0.hook: When she left, I saw her hands had been trembling the whole time.
meal:0.line: 'I made this *meal* small on purpose — a full stomach dulls the spirit.'

vegetable:0.en: Master Qingwu's kitchen held every kind of word-herb, yet tonight her table was plain: steamed rice, clear soup, and a single *vegetable* — a pale green leaf said to calm the mind before great tests. She served it to each of us without explanation. Its taste was clean and faintly sweet, like early morning air.
vegetable:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师尊为我们备下清淡的饭食，桌上只有一碟____，据说能在大考前定心神。
vegetable:0.hook: After we finished, the soup bowl held a tiny silver crack none of us remembered seeing before.
vegetable:0.line: 'Eat this *vegetable* slowly — it carries a calming word-formula within its leaves.'

adopt:0.en: Shen Wujiu pulled out an old scroll and spread it flat on the low table. 'For tonight, *adopt* this breathing form,' he told me, tracing the pattern with one finger. 'Senior disciples used it the night before their own trials. It kept their minds clear until sunrise.' I copied the pattern carefully into my palm.
adopt:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师兄建议我____一种古老的调息法，以便在考验前保持心神清明。
adopt:0.hook: The scroll rolled itself shut the moment I lifted my hand away.
adopt:0.line: '*Adopt* this breathing form tonight and your mind will stay clear until dawn.'

miss:0.en: I looked at the small wooden desk I had used since my first day — the ink stain shaped like a cloud, the tiny chip on the corner. Xiaoxing leaned in the doorway and smiled. 'You will *miss* this room when you rise to the upper peak,' she said, her voice light but her eyes carrying something deeper.
miss:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师妹说我通过考验后一定会____这间简陋的小屋。
miss:0.hook: A gust of wind moved through the closed window, lifting the corner of an unwritten page.
miss:0.line: 'You will *miss* this quiet little room more than you expect, I think.'

yourself:0.en: I had copied the same glyph thirty times when Master Qingwu walked past and paused. She studied my work for a long moment. 'You are writing what you think I want to see,' she said at last. 'Write it for *yourself* instead.' I set down the brush, breathed once, and began again. The thirty-first glyph was different — and right.
yourself:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师尊发现我在迎合她的喜好，告诉我要为____而写，而非为她。
yourself:0.hook: The glyph dried in the shape of a key no one had drawn there.
yourself:0.line: 'Do not write for me — write for *yourself*, and the word-formula will answer.'

century:0.en: Before we parted for the night, Master Qingwu stood at the window and looked out over the sea of clouds. 'This sect has stood for a *century*,' she said quietly, 'because each generation of disciples carried their fear into the trial and came out the other side.' She turned to face us. Her expression was neither proud nor solemn — only steady.
century:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，师尊说这个宗门历经一个____，因为每一代弟子都带着恐惧走进了考验。
century:0.hook: Far below, the sea of clouds parted briefly, revealing a light that should not have been there.
century:0.line: 'For a *century* this sect has endured, and so will you when morning comes.'

responsibility:0.en: Master Qingwu set a single candle on the stone table and looked at each of us in turn. 'Every word-herb you learn carries a *responsibility*,' she said quietly. 'If you use it wrongly, the cloud beneath our mountain will darken.' I pressed my palm flat against the cold stone, feeling the weight of that truth settle into my bones.
responsibility:0.cnHint: 青雾师尊告诫弟子们，习得每一株字草都意味着承担沉重的____。
responsibility:0.hook: Outside, the candle flame bent sideways, though no wind had entered the room.
responsibility:0.line: 'Every word you master carries a *responsibility* you cannot put down.'

soon:0.en: Shen Wujiu rolled out a worn scroll on the inner-hall floor and traced the first formula with one careful finger. 'You will feel nothing now,' he told me, 'but the word will root itself in your spirit, and *soon* it will rise like a herb after rain.' I knelt beside him and read the characters until my eyes blurred.
soon:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，修炼的字诀____就会在心中生根发芽。
soon:0.hook: A low hum rose from the scroll, fading before either of us could name it.
soon:0.line: 'Train with patience — the answer will come *soon* enough.'

center:0.en: The inner hall held a single pillar of white jade, and Master Qingwu said that the oldest word-herb of all rested at its *center*, sealed there long before any of us were born. Xiaoxing pressed her ear to the stone and whispered that she could hear it breathing. I was not sure she was wrong.
center:0.cnHint: 内堂白玉柱的____封印着云海宗最古老的字草。
center:0.hook: A thin crack, no wider than a hair, appeared along the pillar's base.
center:0.line: 'The strongest formula is always sealed at the *center*, where no one thinks to look.'

arrive:0.en: We had been told the trial scrolls would *arrive* before the third bell of night, yet the shelf above the writing table stood empty long after the bell had faded. Xiaoxing lit a second lamp. Shen Wujiu said nothing, only watched the door. The silence in the room grew heavier with every breath.
arrive:0.cnHint: 三更之前，考验弟子的卷轴应当____，但书架依然空空如也。
arrive:0.hook: When the scrolls finally slid under the door, they were already open.
arrive:0.line: 'Tell me the moment the trial scrolls *arrive* — do not wait.'

boost:0.en: Shen Wujiu ground a pale word-herb between two stones and stirred the dust into warm water. 'Drink this before you attempt the night formula,' he said. 'It will *boost* the spirit-channel just enough to hold the word without it burning you.' I drank slowly, feeling a soft warmth climb from my stomach to my throat.
boost:0.cnHint: 师兄调制的字草汤能____灵脉，让弟子安全承载夜咒。
boost:0.hook: The warmth stopped just below my heart and would not rise further.
boost:0.line: 'A small herb at the right moment can *boost* your spirit more than a month of practice.'

conflict:0.en: Two formulas on the open scroll seemed to *conflict* with each other: one called for silence, the other for a spoken tone at the same step. I brought the problem to Master Qingwu, who studied the page for a long moment without speaking. Then she folded it in half and handed it back. 'That tension,' she said, 'is the lesson.'
conflict:0.cnHint: 卷轴上的两条咒诀相互____，我不得不请教师尊。
conflict:0.hook: Master Qingwu's sleeve brushed the ink, and both formulas changed.
conflict:0.line: 'When two paths *conflict*, stop — the answer lives inside the contradiction.'

demand:0.en: The night-formula did not simply ask for focus; it would *demand* every thread of attention I owned and pull hard at them all at once. Master Qingwu had said this plainly during the evening lesson, her voice as calm as still water. I sat cross-legged on the mat, closed my eyes, and tried to gather those threads before the bell rang.
demand:0.cnHint: 夜咒不只是需要专注，它会____习者全部的心神。
demand:0.hook: The bell rang one beat early, and the threads scattered before I was ready.
demand:0.line: 'The highest words *demand* everything — offer less and they will take it anyway.'

emotion:0.en: Xiaoxing told me that the healing word-herb worked best when the one who spoke it felt a clear *emotion* — not sorrow, not joy, but something honest beneath both. She had learned this by accident, she said, when a word she barely knew had mended a cracked stone bowl simply because she had meant it. I held that thought like a lamp through the long study hour.
emotion:0.cnHint: 师妹说，疗愈字草在施咒者怀有真实____时，效力最强。
emotion:0.hook: Near midnight, my own stone bowl developed a crack I had not made.
emotion:0.line: 'Pour a true *emotion* into the word, and the word will pour itself into the world.'

management:0.en: Inside the Hall of Records, I found row after row of jade tablets, each one holding the name of a disciple who had fallen in the great trials. Master Qingwu stood at the centre, her hands folded, speaking in a low voice. 'The *management* of these names is a sacred duty,' she said. 'Each one must be remembered.' A single tablet near the back began to glow without cause.
management:0.cnHint: 在记录殿内，师尊向弟子解释对名册的____是一项神圣职责。
management:0.hook: The glowing tablet bore tomorrow's date.
management:0.line: 'The *management* of these records holds the fate of every disciple.'

perfect:0.en: Shen Wujiu set a small clay jar on the table between us. Inside was a single leaf, preserved in pale golden light. 'This herb reached its *perfect* form only once in a hundred years,' he said quietly. He did not reach for it. Outside, the wind off the cloud sea had gone completely still, and even the candle flame held its breath.
perfect:0.cnHint: 师兄向我展示一株百年才能达到____状态的灵草。
perfect:0.hook: The stillness outside was not peace — it was waiting.
perfect:0.line: 'This leaf reached its *perfect* form tonight, and only tonight.'

along:0.en: I walked *along* the inner corridor of the archive room, trailing my fingers across the cold stone shelves. Xiaoxing followed a step behind, her lantern painting soft shadows on rows of sealed scrolls. 'Each scroll is a word that someone chose to forget,' she told me softly. At the far end of the corridor, one scroll had already been opened — and left that way.
along:0.cnHint: 我和小星____走廊行走，发现一卷本该封存的经文已被人打开。
along:0.hook: Dust on the floor showed only one set of footprints, and they were not ours.
along:0.line: 'Walk *along* this path slowly — some seals here are still alive.'

harm:0.en: Master Qingwu placed both hands over the small cracked formation stone on her desk. 'A word spoken without understanding will *harm* the speaker first,' she said, her tone even and certain. She lifted her hands; the crack had not closed. I understood then that she had not tried to fix it — only to show me what carelessness truly costs. Somewhere below, a bell rang once.
harm:0.cnHint: 师尊告诫我，不理解其含义就贸然使用灵字，只会____自己。
harm:0.hook: The bell below rings only when a disciple's word-bond breaks.
harm:0.line: 'To speak without knowing will *harm* you long before it touches your enemy.'

increasingly:0.en: The candles in the reading room had been burning since dawn, and as the night deepened they became *increasingly* dim, one by one, as though the darkness were drinking the light from the inside out. I pressed my palm to the page I was studying and felt the characters push back against my skin. Shen Wujiu looked up from his own scroll. 'Stop,' he said, very quietly.
increasingly:0.cnHint: 夜深时，书室的烛火____暗淡，我手中的经文突然对我产生了抵触。
increasingly:0.hook: The last candle flickered, and something in the dark leaned closer.
increasingly:0.line: 'The resistance you feel is *increasingly* strong — put the scroll down now.'

opinion:0.en: Xiaoxing spread three herb charts across the low table and looked at me with clear, patient eyes. 'What is your *opinion* on which word-root should anchor the formula?' she asked. I pointed to the middle chart without confidence. She did not say I was wrong; she only turned all three charts face-down. Through the wooden floor, I felt a deep vibration rise and then go silent.
opinion:0.cnHint: 小星询问我对药方根字选择的____，我的回答让她若有所思地翻转了图表。
opinion:0.hook: The vibration in the floor was the mountain breathing — and it had just stopped.
opinion:0.line: 'I want your honest *opinion* before we fix this formula into stone.'

previous:0.en: On the desk lay a tattered notebook that had belonged to the *previous* disciple assigned to this chamber. I turned the pages gently. The later entries were written in smaller and smaller letters, as if the writer had been trying to hide what they knew. The final page held only one word, circled many times. I recognised it: it was the word I had been assigned to study tonight.
previous:0.cnHint: 我翻阅____任弟子留下的笔记，发现最后一页圈出的正是我今晚要研习的灵字。
previous:0.hook: The word on the page was circled in something that was not ink.
previous:0.line: 'The *previous* disciple in this room never finished explaining what they found.'

aim:0.en: Master Qingwu drew a single character on the air with one finger, and it hung there, burning a soft blue. 'The *aim* of every formula is not power,' she said. 'It is clarity.' She closed her fist and the character vanished, leaving a faint smell of rain. On the window ledge behind her, a grey bird I had never seen before landed, turned its head once, and looked at me.
aim:0.cnHint: 师尊以灵字点化，说明修炼一切功法的____并非力量，而是清明。
aim:0.hook: The grey bird had no shadow on the ledge below its feet.
aim:0.line: 'Your *aim* must be understanding — power is only what follows.'

model:0.en: Master Qingwu set a small clay figure on the stone table before us. 'This,' she said, 'is your *model* for the word Breathe — study its posture, and the herb will answer you.' I traced the tiny shoulders, the open palms, and felt something warm stir in my chest. Outside, the evening bell rang once and did not stop.
model:0.cnHint: 师尊用一个泥像作为学习'呼吸'这个词的____，弟子感受到了灵气涌动。
model:0.hook: The bell should have rung only once, but it rang nine times.
model:0.line: 'Let this *model* guide your hand before your voice attempts the word.'

spot:0.en: I was copying herb-names by lamplight when Shen Wujiu leaned over and tapped the page. 'You can *spot* the error, can't you?' he asked quietly. I looked again and saw it — one wrong stroke, and the word for Heal became the word for Sever. My brush trembled. A thin crack appeared in the inkstone on its own.
spot:0.cnHint: 师兄让我____出抄写中的一个错误，那个错误可能导致灵术完全相反。
spot:0.hook: The inkstone cracked without being touched.
spot:0.line: '*Spot* the wrong stroke now, before the word takes root in the air.'

achievement:0.en: Xiaoxing pinned her first completed formula to the inner wall of the study hall, her hands still shaking with joy. 'One small *achievement*,' she whispered, 'but it is mine.' Master Qingwu said nothing, only nodded once. Then the candle flames all leaned east, toward the mountain's dark face, as if pulled by an unseen breath.
achievement:0.cnHint: 师妹完成了自己的第一份灵咒，这个小小的____让她激动不已。
achievement:0.hook: Every candle in the hall bent east, toward the unlit peak.
achievement:0.line: 'This *achievement* is yours alone — guard it well tonight.'

enter:0.en: Master Qingwu stood at the door of the Word Vault and spoke clearly: 'Only those who can name all five root herbs may *enter*.' I breathed, recalled each syllable, and stepped forward into cool air that tasted of pine and old rain. The stone door closed behind me without sound, and the torches inside burned a faint silver.
enter:0.cnHint: 只有能说出五种根本灵草名字的弟子，才能____藏字阁。
enter:0.hook: The silver torches cast shadows that pointed the wrong way.
enter:0.line: 'Speak the five names truly, and you may *enter* without fear.'

eye:0.en: Shen Wujiu told me to write the word Perceive and then close my eyes. I did. When I opened them again, every herb on the shelf had a faint glow I had never noticed before — as if my *eye* had learned a new kind of seeing. Xiaoxing gasped beside me. On the window paper, a moth printed its shadow and was gone.
eye:0.cnHint: 在练习'感知'这个词后，弟子的____仿佛获得了看见灵光的新能力。
eye:0.hook: A moth left its shadow on the paper and vanished into light.
eye:0.line: 'Train the *eye* before the tongue — what you cannot see, you cannot name.'

shift:0.en: Halfway through the night recitation, I felt a *shift* in the air — the warmth in the room moved, like a tide turning, and the words on my page rearranged their glow from gold to pale blue. Shen Wujiu stiffened beside me but said nothing. Far below the mountain, something large moved through the sea of clouds.
shift:0.cnHint: 夜间诵读时，弟子感受到空气中的一种____，灵文的光芒也随之改变了颜色。
shift:0.hook: Something vast and slow moved beneath the sea of clouds.
shift:0.line: 'Feel the *shift* before it reaches the words, or it will rewrite them.'

agree:0.en: Xiaoxing wanted to practice the word Storm inside the hall; Shen Wujiu shook his head. I found myself caught between them until Master Qingwu asked for my view. 'I *agree* with Shen Wujiu,' I said carefully. 'The hall is too small for storm-words.' Master Qingwu closed her book. The window flew open on its own, and cold air poured in.
agree:0.cnHint: 在争论是否在室内练习'风暴'一词时，弟子选择____师兄的意见。
agree:0.hook: The window flew open the moment I spoke, letting in cold night air.
agree:0.line: 'I *agree* — a storm-word spoken indoors will not forgive the walls.'

aware:0.en: I was almost asleep at my desk when I became *aware* of a sound beneath the silence — a low hum rising from the floorboards, as if the mountain itself were breathing a word too large for any throat. I sat up straight, brush still in hand. The ink in my stone had dried into the shape of an eye.
aware:0.cnHint: 弟子在快睡着时突然____到地板下传来一种低沉的嗡鸣，仿佛山体本身在低语。
aware:0.hook: The dried ink had formed a perfect, unblinking eye.
aware:0.line: 'Be *aware* of what the mountain says before it decides to say it louder.'

land:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled an old scroll across the stone table. It showed every floating peak of the Cloud Sea Sect, each one a circle of *land* torn from the earth long ago by ancient words. 'Study this,' she said. 'Know where you stand before you dare to fly.'
land:0.cnHint: 师尊展开一幅古卷，上面绘有云海宗各处飘浮的____，叮嘱弟子先认清脚下之地再谈飞行。
land:0.hook: At the scroll's edge, one peak had no name — only a red warning stroke.
land:0.line: 'Each circle of *land* on this map was claimed by a word no living disciple can still pronounce.'

promote:0.en: Shen Wujiu lit three incense sticks before the rank board on the inner hall wall. 'A good result in tomorrow's trial will *promote* you from outer to inner disciple,' he said quietly. He did not say what a poor result would bring. The smoke rose, then bent sharply sideways.
promote:0.cnHint: 师兄在内堂名榜前告诉我，明日的试炼若表现出色，就能____我晋升为内门弟子。
promote:0.hook: The smoke bent toward the door that led to the sealed archive.
promote:0.line: 'One strong word spoken with full intent will *promote* you past three ranks at once.'

purchase:0.en: In the sect's exchange hall, Xiaoxing held up a small blue vial. 'This herb-word costs forty spirit points,' she said. 'Your *purchase* of it now will save you pain later.' I turned the vial over in my palm. The word inside glowed like a trapped firefly, waiting to be learned.
purchase:0.cnHint: 师妹在换取堂提醒我，现在____这瓶草字灵药，将来会省去不少苦头。
purchase:0.hook: Behind the counter, the keeper watched me with eyes that did not blink.
purchase:0.line: 'Your *purchase* of a healing word before the trial is the only wisdom I can offer you.'

rely:0.en: The night before the trial, I sat alone in the practice room, palms flat on the cold floor. Master Qingwu had warned me not to *rely* on the words others had given me. 'Shape your own formula,' she had said. 'Borrowed power breaks at the worst moment.' A low bell rang somewhere below the clouds.
rely:0.cnHint: 师尊提醒我，明日试炼不能____别人传授的字诀，要锻造属于自己的法力。
rely:0.hook: The bell rang once more — but there was no bell tower on this peak.
rely:0.line: 'Do not *rely* on my word-gifts during the trial — I will not be there to catch you.'

connect:0.en: Shen Wujiu drew two glowing characters in the air and pressed them together. 'Watch how the roots *connect*,' he said. When the two words touched, a soft green light spread across the ceiling like dawn. 'This is how a healing formula is born — two truths joined into one.' My brush hand trembled with want.
connect:0.cnHint: 师兄演示如何将两个字诀的根脉____在一起，合成一道疗愈法术。
connect:0.hook: The green light faded — except for one thread that drifted toward my sleeve.
connect:0.line: 'If you can *connect* these two words without dropping either, you are ready for tomorrow.'

indicate:0.en: Master Qingwu set five small stones on the table, each carved with a word I did not yet know. 'The color of the stone will *indicate* which element the word commands,' she said. Four glowed steady. The fifth flickered, and she did not explain why she placed it closest to me.
indicate:0.cnHint: 师尊用五块刻字石向我说明，石头的颜色____着该字诀所掌控的灵元属性。
indicate:0.hook: The flickering stone cast a shadow shaped like a hand reaching upward.
indicate:0.line: 'The weight of the stone will *indicate* how much of your spirit it will ask in return.'

period:0.en: 'You have one *period* of incense-time to copy all three formulas,' Xiaoxing said, setting a lit stick beside my desk. Its smoke was thin and fast. I pressed my brush to the paper and felt the words push back, as if they were not yet willing to be written. Half the stick was already ash.
period:0.cnHint: 师妹告知我只有一____香的时间来抄录三份法诀，香烛已经燃了一半。
period:0.hook: When the ash fell, it formed a shape on the desk that looked like a warning glyph.
period:0.line: 'One *period* of focus now will decide what kind of disciple you become by dawn.'

picture:0.en: On the wall of the preparation room hung a large *picture* of the Cloud Sea Sect as it looked a hundred years ago. Three peaks shown in it no longer existed. Shen Wujiu stood before it a long time without speaking. 'Every peak you see was held by a word,' he finally said. 'Some words were forgotten.'
picture:0.cnHint: 备考室墙上挂着一幅百年前云海宗的____，画中有三座山峰如今已不复存在。
picture:0.hook: In the bottom corner of the picture, a small figure stood alone on a peak now gone.
picture:0.line: 'This *picture* does not show you what was lost — only what was left behind.'

relate:0.en: Master Qingwu lit a single candle and told me to sit. 'Before you touch any word-herb,' she said, 'you must learn to *relate* each one to the breath inside you. A herb without a body to answer it is just dust.' I traced the first character slowly, and for one moment the flame leaned toward my finger.
relate:0.cnHint: 师尊让我学会将每味字草与自身气息____，烛火随之微微倾斜。
relate:0.hook: The candle bent again — though no wind had entered the room.
relate:0.line: 'You must *relate* every word to the breath already living in you.'

attitude:0.en: Shen Wujiu found me slouched over my practice scroll at midnight. He straightened my spine with one light touch. 'Your *attitude* shapes the word before your brush does,' he said quietly. I sat tall, wrote the same character again, and this time a faint green mist rose from the ink.
attitude:0.cnHint: 师兄纠正我的____，说姿态先于笔意，随后墨迹升起淡淡绿雾。
attitude:0.hook: The mist drifted upward and did not fade until dawn.
attitude:0.line: 'Your *attitude* at the desk is the first word you write tonight.'

fill:0.en: Xiaoxing handed me a small jade bowl before the evening lesson. 'Let your breath *fill* every corner of the character,' she whispered, 'the way water fills a valley — slowly, without force.' I breathed out, and the ink spread to the very edge of each stroke on its own.
fill:0.cnHint: 师妹让我用气息将字的每个角落____满，墨迹随之自行蔓延至笔画边缘。
fill:0.hook: At the last stroke, the bowl in her hand chimed once, though she had not touched it.
fill:0.line: 'Let your breath *fill* every corner before your brush lifts.'

ignore:0.en: The hall was cold and the other disciples had gone to sleep. I chose to *ignore* the chill and kept copying the healing word until my fingers ached. By the third hour, something warm settled into my palm — not from any fire, but from the word itself.
ignore:0.cnHint: 我____寒意坚持抄写疗愈字符，第三个时辰后掌心升起莫名暖意。
ignore:0.hook: Outside, a low bell rang — yet the Sect's bells were not lit that night.
ignore:0.line: 'To *ignore* the cold and keep writing — that is how a word becomes yours.'

necessary:0.en: Master Qingwu spread twelve word-herbs on the stone table and removed three of them. 'Not every formula is *necessary*,' she said. 'Strength lies in knowing what to leave out.' I stared at the nine that remained, feeling each one pull at the air like a held breath.
necessary:0.cnHint: 师尊移去多余字草，说明知道什么____保留才是真正的力量。
necessary:0.hook: The removed three began to glow softly on the far edge of the table.
necessary:0.line: 'Only what is *necessary* survives the storm — remember that before dawn.'

definitely:0.en: Shen Wujiu read my practice scroll and nodded once. 'This character will *definitely* hold under pressure,' he said, 'but the one beside it will break.' I looked again and saw it — a hairline gap in the second stroke, thin as a spider's thread, that I had missed for three days.
definitely:0.cnHint: 师兄指出我的一个字____能承压，而旁边的字却藏有一处细微裂隙。
definitely:0.hook: Before I could dip my brush, the flawed character faded from the scroll by itself.
definitely:0.line: 'This form will *definitely* hold — but only if you close that gap tonight.'

forget:0.en: 'Whatever you do,' Xiaoxing said, pulling my sleeve before I entered the archive, 'do not *forget* to seal the scroll when you finish. An open word-herb draws what it names.' I nodded, stepped inside, and smelled something I could not place — like rain on warm stone, or a word spoken too soon.
forget:0.cnHint: 师妹叮嘱我绝不能____封存字卷，否则字草会召来它所命名之物。
forget:0.hook: Behind me, the archive door sealed itself before I reached the first shelf.
forget:0.line: 'Do not *forget* to seal the scroll — the word inside is already listening.'

particularly:0.en: Master Qingwu reviewed every disciple's work that evening, but she paused *particularly* long at mine — not at the strong strokes, but at a small character I had written in the corner as a test. She said nothing. She only touched it once with one finger, and it turned silver.
particularly:0.cnHint: 师尊检阅众弟子功课时，____在我角落那个试写的小字旁停留许久，指触后它变为银色。
particularly:0.hook: Silver ink, the eldest disciples whispered later, only appears the night before the sky cracks.
particularly:0.line: 'I stopped *particularly* at yours — that small word in the corner knows something.'

meanwhile:0.en: Inside the Pill Hall, I arranged rows of spirit herbs on a stone table. Master Qingwu traced each leaf with one careful finger. *Meanwhile*, Shen Wujiu stood at the window, watching the sky turn the colour of old bronze. None of us spoke. The silence itself felt like a held breath.
meanwhile:0.cnHint: 在丹堂内，师尊检验灵草，我整理药材，____，师兄凝视着异色的天空。
meanwhile:0.hook: Outside, the first cloud split open like a wound.
meanwhile:0.line: '*Meanwhile*, keep your hands steady — the herbs feel every tremor you carry.'

damage:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled the sect's oldest scroll across the floor of the archive room. Brown edges crumbled at his touch. 'Look,' he said quietly. The *damage* was not from age alone — something had burned through three lines of the healing formula, leaving only ash and silence where the cure once lived.
damage:0.cnHint: 在藏经阁，师兄展开古卷，发现关键药方遭到了____，三行字化为灰烬。
damage:0.hook: Whoever erased those words had not wanted the sick to be saved.
damage:0.line: 'The *damage* to this scroll means someone feared what it could heal.'

police:0.en: Master Qingwu gathered all disciples in the inner hall. She stood straight, her voice level. 'On a mountain above clouds, we have no *police* to keep order,' she said. 'Each of us is the law we choose to honour.' I wrote those words on my palm in invisible ink, hoping they would last.
police:0.cnHint: 师尊在内堂集合弟子，告诫我们云海山上没有____，每个人都是自己所遵守的律法。
police:0.hook: One disciple in the back row did not meet her eyes.
police:0.line: 'We have no *police* here — only the vows we make and the ones we break.'

race:0.en: Xiaoxing burst through the library door, her robe dusted with chalk. 'It is a *race*,' she said, spreading a map on the desk. 'Five sects are all seeking the same sky-root herb before dawn.' I looked at the marked paths and felt my pulse rise like water before a storm.
race:0.cnHint: 小星冲进书房，说明这是一场____——五大门派都在争夺同一株天根灵草。
race:0.hook: Dawn, it turned out, was only three hours away.
race:0.line: 'This *race* will not be won by the fastest feet, but the clearest mind.'

medical:0.en: The sect's *medical* hall smelled of pine smoke and dried lotus root. I sat beside a low lamp, copying a formula for cloud-fever into my notebook. Each herb had a rank: some healed gently, some struck hard. Master Qingwu had written in the margin: 'Power without patience poisons the hand that holds it.'
medical:0.cnHint: 在门派的____堂中，我抄录治疗云热症的药方，师尊在旁边写下了警示之语。
medical:0.hook: The last herb on the list had no known cure for its side effects.
medical:0.line: 'Every *medical* formula here was paid for by someone's suffering — copy carefully.'

wear:0.en: Three days before the heavenly trial, the spirit stone above our gate began to *wear* thin. Its once-bright surface had turned the grey of cold ash. Shen Wujiu pressed his palm to it and pulled his hand back fast, as though the stone had whispered something none of us were ready to hear.
wear:0.cnHint: 天劫前三天，山门上的灵石开始____，颜色变得如冷灰一般黯淡。
wear:0.hook: A stone that whispers is a stone that is almost done speaking.
wear:0.line: 'Watch how the carvings *wear* away — the mountain is trying to warn us.'

climate:0.en: Master Qingwu stood before the long map of the Cloud Sea. She pointed to where the mist had once been steady and soft. 'The *climate* of the upper peaks has shifted,' she said. 'What fed our herbs for a hundred years now burns them.' I looked at the withered rows outside and understood.
climate:0.cnHint: 师尊指着云海图说，高峰的____已经改变，曾滋养灵草百年之物如今却灼伤了它们。
climate:0.hook: A sect whose herbs die has already begun to fall.
climate:0.line: 'The *climate* here has changed — our old formulas may no longer hold.'

head:0.en: Shen Wujiu sat at the *head* of the long study table, the trial manual open before him. He did not look like someone who was afraid. But his brush had not moved in an hour, and the inkstone had gone dry. Xiaoxing and I said nothing. We simply lit a second lamp and sat beside him.
head:0.cnHint: 师兄坐在长桌____，天劫手册摆在眼前，但他的笔已一个时辰未曾动过。
head:0.hook: An untouched page on the eve of trial says more than any word.
head:0.line: 'Sit at the *head* of your fear tonight, or it will sit at yours come dawn.'

return:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old pine and dried cloud-moss. Master Qingwu set a worn scroll on the low table and said the lesson for tonight was not about flying. 'Every word you release into the wind must find its *return* to your own heart before it becomes power,' she said. The lamp flame did not flicker — yet somehow it burned lower.
return:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，每一个字在变成力量之前，都必须先____到自己的内心。
return:0.hook: The scroll's last line had been written in ash, not ink.
return:0.line: 'Every word must find its *return* to your heart before it has power.'

remove:0.en: Shen Wujiu knelt beside me on the stone floor of the archive room, studying a formula carved into a jade plate. 'You cannot simply *remove* a word from a living formula,' he said quietly, 'the way you pull a weed from soil. The root stays. The pain stays.' Outside, the wind through the mountain pass had stopped without warning.
remove:0.cnHint: 师兄警告我，不能随意从活的法诀中____一个字，因为根和痛苦会留下来。
remove:0.hook: The jade plate had begun to feel warm in my hands.
remove:0.line: 'You cannot simply *remove* a word from a living formula — the root stays.'

colleague:0.en: Xiaoxing spread her herb-charts across the reading table and pointed to my name written in the margin. 'A new *colleague* earns trust by listening before speaking,' she said, not unkindly. I nodded and copied her careful brushwork until the candle burned to its last finger of wax. Then a thin crack ran across the stone wall behind her charts.
colleague:0.cnHint: 师妹说，一位新____要先倾听再开口，才能赢得信任。
colleague:0.hook: The crack in the wall traced the exact shape of a flying crane.
colleague:0.line: 'A new *colleague* earns trust by listening before speaking.'

normal:0.en: I asked Master Qingwu whether it was *normal* for a word-seed to glow before a storm. She set down her brush and looked at me for a long moment. 'Nothing in the Cloud Sea Sect is normal,' she said at last, 'only familiar or unfamiliar.' That night every word-seed in the storage jars glowed at once, cold and blue.
normal:0.cnHint: 我问师尊，字种在暴风雨前发光是否____，她给了我一个意味深长的回答。
normal:0.hook: Every word-seed in the hall glowed cold blue at the same moment.
normal:0.line: 'Nothing here is *normal* — only familiar or unfamiliar.'

succeed:0.en: Shen Wujiu had failed the Cloud-Step formula three times. On the fourth attempt he stood very still, breathed once, and spoke the word softly. He rose half a foot above the floor. 'To *succeed*,' he told me after landing, 'you must stop trying to force the word and let it choose you.' A low sound, like distant thunder, rolled up from below the clouds.
succeed:0.cnHint: 师兄成功悬浮后告诉我，要想____，就必须让字选择你，而不是强迫它。
succeed:0.hook: Distant thunder rose from far beneath the sea of clouds.
succeed:0.line: 'To *succeed*, you must let the word choose you, not force it.'

image:0.en: Master Qingwu asked me to hold the character for 'wind' in my mind and describe what I saw. I said I saw nothing. She shook her head. 'The *image* that rises before the word leaves your mouth — that is the true formula,' she said. 'Without it, you are only making noise.' The ink in the practice dish rippled though no one had touched it.
image:0.cnHint: 师尊说，字离口之前心中浮现的____才是真正的法诀。
image:0.hook: The ink rippled in the still dish as if something breathed beneath it.
image:0.line: 'The *image* that rises before the word leaves your mouth — that is the true formula.'

ourselves:0.en: Xiaoxing and I carried the heavy cloud-jars from the lower shelf and set them in a row for tomorrow's ritual. 'We have only *ourselves* to rely on tonight,' she said, glancing at the empty teacher's seat. 'Master Qingwu will not return until dawn.' A single jar, sealed tight, began to hum in the dark like a living thing.
ourselves:0.cnHint: 师尊未归，师妹说今晚我们只能依靠____。
ourselves:0.hook: One sealed jar hummed softly in the dark, though no one had touched it.
ourselves:0.line: 'We have only *ourselves* to rely on tonight — Master Qingwu will not return until dawn.'

catch:0.en: The practice word slipped from my breath too fast and drifted toward the open window like a spark. Shen Wujiu stepped forward and closed his hand around the air. 'You must *catch* a runaway word before it seeds itself in the wrong soil,' he said, opening his palm to show nothing there. At the window, a moth landed on the sill and did not move again.
catch:0.cnHint: 师兄说，必须在逃跑的字落入错误土壤之前____住它。
catch:0.hook: A moth landed on the windowsill and sat perfectly still, as if listening.
catch:0.line: 'You must *catch* a runaway word before it seeds itself in the wrong soil.'

mistake:0.en: The inner hall smelled of dried herbs and old ink. I copied the healing formula onto rice paper, careful with every stroke. But one character curved the wrong way, and the paper began to smoke. 'A single *mistake* in a formula can turn medicine into poison,' Master Qingwu said, lifting the charred page. She did not raise her voice. She did not need to. Outside, the wind across the mountain peak fell suddenly, completely still.
mistake:0.cnHint: 我在抄写治愈符文时写错了一笔，导致纸张开始冒烟，师尊平静地提醒我一个____的后果。
mistake:0.hook: The silence that followed felt heavier than any storm.
mistake:0.line: 'A single *mistake* in a formula can turn medicine into poison.'

staff:0.en: Master Qingwu gathered all of us in the archive hall. Every elder, every senior disciple, every keeper of the seed-word vaults stood in a long row. 'The full *staff* of this sect holds one breath before a trial,' she said, her voice low and even. I counted eighteen people and felt very small. Then the lanterns along the far wall dimmed, one by one, without any wind.
staff:0.cnHint: 师尊将门派所有____聚集在典藏殿，宣布在天劫前共同屏息等待考验。
staff:0.hook: The last lantern dimmed, and no one moved to relight it.
staff:0.line: 'The full *staff* of this sect holds one breath before a trial.'

enhance:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a small jade slip carved with the word 'bright.' 'Speak it slowly into the ink,' he said. I did, and the characters on my practice scroll began to glow a soft gold. 'Certain words *enhance* the ones around them,' he explained, 'the way one good herb lifts the whole formula.' I read the page again, and this time the meaning opened like a door. A thin crack of blue light ran along the windowsill and was gone.
enhance:0.cnHint: 师兄教我用一个特定的词来____周围的文字，让整篇符文焕发光芒。
enhance:0.hook: The blue crack sealed itself, but the air still hummed.
enhance:0.line: 'Certain words *enhance* the ones around them, the way one herb lifts a formula.'

famous:0.en: Xiaoxing spread an old scroll across the study table. 'This is the Dew-Root Codex,' she whispered. 'It is *famous* even among the highest peaks — no disciple below the third ring has ever read it through.' The characters on the page shifted as I leaned close, as if they were deciding whether to let me see them. I pulled back. Somewhere deep inside the mountain, a bell rang once, though no hand had touched it.
famous:0.cnHint: 师妹向我展示了一部____的古老典籍，据说连三环以下弟子都无缘读完它。
famous:0.hook: The bell rang once more, deeper, from somewhere no bell should be.
famous:0.line: 'This codex is *famous* even among the highest peaks — read it carefully.'

project:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long chart on the central table. It showed twelve words arranged in a circle, each connected by fine lines to the others. 'Your first *project* is to learn these twelve words as a single living system, not as a list,' she said. Each word, I realised, was also a kind of door. I touched the edge of the chart and felt a faint warmth rise through my fingers. Above the hall, a cloud shaped like an open hand drifted slowly past the window.
project:0.cnHint: 师尊布置了第一个____，要求我把十二个词作为一个整体来掌握，而非逐一死记。
project:0.hook: The cloud-hand paused outside the window, fingers spread wide.
project:0.line: 'Your first *project* is to learn these twelve words as one living system.'

record:0.en: The archive keeper, Shen Wujiu, showed me the oldest logbook on the lowest shelf. Every disciple who had ever spoken a word formula for the first time had their result written inside. 'This *record* goes back three hundred years,' he said quietly, tracing one faded line. My own name was already at the bottom of the final page, written in ink that still looked wet. I had not written it there. No one in the room had.
record:0.cnHint: 师兄向我展示了一本三百年历史的古老____，而我的名字已经出现在最后一页，墨迹未干。
record:0.hook: The wet ink caught the lamplight, and my name seemed to breathe.
record:0.line: 'This *record* holds every first spoken formula for three hundred years.'

regular:0.en: 'You will follow a *regular* schedule from tonight,' Master Qingwu told me, setting a small wooden board on my desk. Dawn practice, midday reading, dusk recitation — the same pattern, every day, until the words lived in my bones rather than my memory. I nodded and looked at the board. The characters for 'dusk recitation' had been written darker than the rest, as though pressed harder, or perhaps as though the brush had trembled. Master Qingwu had already turned away and offered no explanation.
regular:0.cnHint: 师尊要求我从今晚起遵循一套____的修炼时间表，但黄昏诵读那栏的笔迹明显更深。
regular:0.hook: The darker characters seemed to pulse once, then went still.
regular:0.line: 'You will follow a *regular* schedule from tonight — same pattern, every day.'

whatever:0.en: Master Qingwu set a single candle on the stone table and told us to sit. 'Tonight,' she said, '*whatever* word rises in your mind, write it on the paper before you.' I wrote 'sky.' Shen Wujiu wrote 'weight.' Xiaoxing wrote nothing — her brush trembled above the page.
whatever:0.cnHint: 师尊要求弟子把脑海中____浮现的字写下来，小星的笔却颤抖着迟迟未落。
whatever:0.hook: The candle flame bent toward Xiaoxing's empty page, as if reading it.
whatever:0.line: '*Whatever* word you fear most is the word you must write first,' said Master Qingwu.

predict:0.en: In the archive hall, Shen Wujiu unrolled an old chart of cloud patterns. 'The elders use these to *predict* which words will bloom this season,' he said quietly, tracing a spiral with one finger. The chart showed a storm forming — one that had no name in any language I had yet learned.
predict:0.cnHint: 师兄展开古老的云图，说前辈用它来____哪些词语本季将会盛开，图上有一场无名的风暴。
predict:0.hook: The spiral on the chart was still moving, slowly, on its own.
predict:0.line: 'No one can *predict* when a word chooses its disciple,' Shen Wujiu said softly.

road:0.en: The inner hall held a long painting: a single *road* rising through cloud layers toward a peak lost in white mist. Master Qingwu said every word we mastered would add one stone to that road. I counted the stones already there. There were thousands — and the peak was still hidden.
road:0.cnHint: 大厅里的画中有一条通往云端山顶的____，师尊说每掌握一个词就添一块石头，山顶仍藏在雾中。
road:0.hook: One stone near the top glowed faintly red, warm as a warning.
road:0.line: 'The *road* to the summit is made of words, not steps,' Master Qingwu said.

solution:0.en: Xiaoxing had been struggling with the word 'still' for three days, unable to hold its meaning steady. At last she sat cross-legged on the cold floor, closed her eyes, and breathed until the room felt like water. Silence was her *solution*. When she opened her eyes, the word floated above her palm, calm and bright.
solution:0.cnHint: 小星苦学"still"三日无果，最终用静坐的方式找到了____，让词语安稳地悬浮在掌心。
solution:0.hook: But the word flickered once, as though something unseen had brushed against it.
solution:0.line: 'Stillness itself is the *solution* when a word refuses to settle,' Xiaoxing said.

total:0.en: Master Qingwu asked each of us to count the words we had truly mastered — not memorized, but felt in bone and breath. My *total* was seven. Shen Wujiu said nothing, only smiled. Xiaoxing counted on her fingers twice and looked troubled. Seven, the master said, was both a beginning and a warning.
total:0.cnHint: 师尊要我们清点真正掌握的词语____数，七个既是起点也是警示。
total:0.hook: Shen Wujiu's smile faded the moment Master Qingwu turned away.
total:0.line: 'A *total* of seven is enough to survive one trial — barely,' Master Qingwu said.

fail:0.en: Shen Wujiu showed me the test of the mirror word: you speak it aloud, and if your will is weak, the word turns against you. 'Many disciples *fail* this test not from lack of skill, but from doubt,' he said, adjusting the lamp. Outside, the wind had stopped. That sudden silence felt like a held breath.
fail:0.cnHint: 师兄说许多弟子____镜词之试，并非因为技艺不足，而是因为内心有疑。
fail:0.hook: Somewhere below the mountain, a bell rang — once, at the wrong hour.
fail:0.line: 'It is no shame to *fail* a test; it is shame to stop after failing,' said Shen Wujiu.

function:0.en: Master Qingwu placed two identical leaves on the table. 'Same plant, different words written on each,' she said. One healed a cut on my hand in seconds. The other did nothing. 'The *function* of a word,' she told us, 'depends entirely on who holds it.' The healed skin felt warmer than the rest of my hand.
function:0.cnHint: 师尊用两片写有不同词语的叶子演示：词语的____取决于持有者本身。
function:0.hook: The leaf that had failed to heal slowly turned black at its edge.
function:0.line: 'The *function* of any word changes when fear enters the speaker,' Master Qingwu said.

method:0.en: Late in the study hall, I asked Shen Wujiu how he learned so many words so quickly. He thought for a long time before answering. 'My *method* is simple,' he said at last. 'I treat each word as a living thing and ask what it needs from me.' He closed his book. Through the window, a cloud shaped like an open hand drifted past.
method:0.cnHint: 师兄透露自己快速习词的____：把每个词当作有生命的东西，问它需要什么。
method:0.hook: The cloud hand paused outside the window, fingers slowly curling closed.
method:0.line: 'Find your own *method*; copying mine will only slow you down,' Shen Wujiu said.

review:0.en: The night before the great trial, I spread every scroll I had copied that month across the stone floor. A *review* of all the words I had learned — each one a living herb glowing faintly in the dark — filled me with quiet courage. Master Qingwu had said that a word forgotten in the trial was a wound that would not close.
review:0.cnHint: 天劫前夜，我将习得的所有词语____了一遍，内心逐渐平静。
review:0.hook: Then one scroll began to burn at its edges, all on its own.
review:0.line: 'A careful *review* tonight may be the only thing that saves you tomorrow,' said Master Qingwu.

ahead:0.en: Shen Wujiu set a single candle on the table between us and looked at me with calm eyes. 'The trial is *ahead* of us,' he said, 'but the path only opens for those who have already walked it in their minds.' I closed my eyes and traced every word-formula I knew, step by careful step.
ahead:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，考验就在____，我们必须做好准备。
ahead:0.hook: Outside, the clouds beneath the mountain turned a deep and warning red.
ahead:0.line: 'The hardest part of the trial lies *ahead*, so rest your mind now,' said Shen Wujiu.

cheap:0.en: Xiaoxing showed me a small jar of low-grade ink she had found in the supply room. 'The *cheap* ink fades before the word can take root,' she warned, uncapping it so I could smell its thin, weak scent. I put it aside and reached for the good ink Master Qingwu had given me on the first day.
cheap:0.cnHint: 师妹提醒我，____的墨水会让词语在扎根之前就消散。
cheap:0.hook: A faint hiss rose from the jar as she set it down, as if something inside disagreed.
cheap:0.line: 'Never write a word-formula with *cheap* ink — it will fail you when you need it most,' said Xiaoxing.

critical:0.en: Master Qingwu walked slowly among us as we practised, pausing longest at my desk. The word I was tracing was 'ascend,' and she said it was the most *critical* of all the trial formulas — the one that carried a disciple from the lower cloud-shelf to the peak altar. I pressed my brush more firmly to the page.
critical:0.cnHint: 师尊告诉我，'ascend'这个词是试炼中最____的法诀。
critical:0.hook: The candle flame leaned toward my page, as though it too was waiting to see if I would succeed.
critical:0.line: 'This word is *critical* — write it wrong once and the clouds will not hold you,' said Master Qingwu.

motivate:0.en: I had been staring at the same page for so long that the characters blurred. Then Xiaoxing slid a small note under my hand: 'Remember why you climbed here.' That single line was enough to *motivate* me more than any reward or threat could have. I dipped my brush and began again with steady strokes.
motivate:0.cnHint: 师妹的一句话____了我，让我重新提起笔，认真书写。
motivate:0.hook: At that moment the mountain gave a low rumble, as if it approved.
motivate:0.line: 'I wrote this note because I knew it would *motivate* you when nothing else could,' said Xiaoxing.

charge:0.en: Shen Wujiu explained that the sect would not *charge* us any fee for using the inner library tonight — that privilege was granted only on the eve of a trial. I gathered my scrolls quickly and climbed the narrow steps, knowing the doors would seal again at dawn and the words inside would go back to sleep.
charge:0.cnHint: 师兄说，今晚宗门不会向我们____使用内库的费用。
charge:0.hook: As I entered, the shelves rearranged themselves with a soft, deliberate sound.
charge:0.line: 'The sect will not *charge* you tonight — use every hour the library gives you,' said Shen Wujiu.

complex:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled the final scroll and I felt my breath catch. The healing formula drawn there was far more *complex* than anything I had studied — layer upon layer of words wound around each other like roots beneath a mountain, each one depending on the one below. I would have to learn all of it before dawn.
complex:0.cnHint: 师尊展开最后一卷，上面的法诀远比我想象的更____。
complex:0.hook: The scroll then rolled itself back up, as if daring me to try again.
complex:0.line: 'Do not be afraid — *complex* as it looks, every layer has its own simple truth,' said Master Qingwu.

itself:0.en: I had memorised every word-formula, yet the trial worried me *itself* — not the words, but the silence between them, where a disciple's courage either held or did not. Shen Wujiu told me that the mountain tested the person, not the knowledge, and that understanding had always been more useful than memory.
itself:0.cnHint: 我已背熟所有法诀，但试炼____让我感到不安，不仅仅是因为词语的难度。
itself:0.hook: Then the mountain bell rang once, an hour before it was ever supposed to ring.
itself:0.line: 'The trial *itself* is not your enemy — your own doubt is,' said Shen Wujiu.

join:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long scroll across the stone table. 'Every word you have learned this season must *join* the others,' she said, 'or the formula breaks like a snapped branch.' I pressed my fingertip to the first character and felt the whole line hum. Outside, the evening bell had not yet rung — but it should have, an hour ago.
join:0.cnHint: 师尊说，所有学过的字必须____在一起，否则法诀会断裂。
join:0.hook: The bell tower stood silent, and no one could explain why.
join:0.line: 'Let each word *join* the next, or the whole formula will fail.'

significant:0.en: Shen Wujiu set a small jade bottle on the shelf beside my bed. 'This word — preserve — is more *significant* than it looks,' he said softly. 'Master Qingwu used it once to hold back a storm for three days.' I turned the bottle over in my palm. A single dark crack ran along its base.
significant:0.cnHint: 师兄说，'preserve'这个字比看起来更____，师尊曾用它阻挡暴风雨。
significant:0.hook: The crack in the jade had not been there that morning.
significant:0.line: 'That word is far more *significant* than you think, junior.'

step:0.en: Xiaoxing taught me to *step* across the practice room without making a sound — each foot placed where the old floorboards would not cry out. 'The room remembers,' she whispered. When we reached the far wall, I saw words carved there in a hand I did not know, glowing faint gold in the candlelight.
step:0.cnHint: 师妹教我如何____过练功室，不发出任何声音，直到我们发现了墙上发光的字。
step:0.hook: The carved words had not appeared on any map of the sect.
step:0.line: '*Step* lightly — the room listens to every sound you make.'

unique:0.en: Among all the words painted on the inner wall of the library, one was *unique*: it had no partner, no opposite, no family of related terms beside it. Master Qingwu said nothing when I pointed to it. She only closed her eyes, and the candle flame bent toward that word as if leaning in to listen.
unique:0.cnHint: 图书馆内墙上有一个____的字，没有同类，没有对应词，烛焰向它弯去。
unique:0.hook: When Master Qingwu opened her eyes, her pupils held a faint silver light.
unique:0.line: 'That word is *unique* — it stands alone for a reason, disciple.'

inside:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a hollow wooden sphere no larger than a peach. 'The formula is written *inside*,' he said. 'Do not open it with your hands.' I held it to the light, and through the thin walls I could see characters moving — slowly, like fish beneath ice. Then one of them stopped and faced me.
inside:0.cnHint: 师兄给了我一个木球，说法诀写在____，我看见里面的字在移动。
inside:0.hook: One character had turned to face outward, as if it had chosen to be read.
inside:0.line: 'The answer you need is written *inside* — use your breath, not your hands.'

majority:0.en: When Master Qingwu tested the new disciples, the *majority* of them could light a single character with one breath. I managed three, then coughed smoke. She made no remark, only wrote something in her small notebook. Later I saw that Xiaoxing had lit none at all — yet Master Qingwu had smiled at her longest.
majority:0.cnHint: 师尊测试时，大____弟子能点亮一个字，而我点亮了三个，师尊却对师妹笑得最久。
majority:0.hook: What Master Qingwu wrote in that notebook, no one was permitted to see.
majority:0.line: 'The *majority* pass this test, but passing is not the same as understanding.'

notice:0.en: I began to *notice* something odd in the third week: the words on my practice scroll shifted position each night, only slightly, like seeds settling in soil. I said nothing to Master Qingwu. I drew a small dot beside each character before sleep, and by morning every dot had moved three brushstrokes to the left.
notice:0.cnHint: 我开始____到一件奇怪的事：练习卷轴上的字每晚都会稍微移动位置。
notice:0.hook: By the seventh morning, all the dots had formed a single straight line pointing north.
notice:0.line: 'Did you *notice* the scroll moved again last night, junior sister?'

taste:0.en: Master Qingwu said that every word has a *taste* if you speak it the right way. Healing words are said to be cool, like river water. I tried the word for 'sky' and felt something sharp and clean at the back of my throat — then a warmth spreading into my chest that did not belong to any food I had ever eaten.
taste:0.cnHint: 师尊说每个字都有____，我尝试发出'天'字，感受到了一种陌生的温热。
taste:0.hook: The warmth stayed in my chest until midnight, then vanished all at once.
taste:0.line: 'Every word has a *taste*, disciple — learn to feel it before you speak it.'

differ:0.en: Master Qingwu laid two scrolls before me. 'Read both before dawn,' she said. The healing formula and the flight formula seemed alike at first, but I soon saw how they *differ*: one draws energy inward, the other releases it outward. I copied the distinction carefully into my notes.
differ:0.cnHint: 师尊让我比较两卷功法，我发现它们在运气方向上____很大。
differ:0.hook: By midnight, a third scroll had appeared — and no one had entered the room.
differ:0.line: 'Notice how these two paths *differ* at the very first breath of energy.'

shape:0.en: Shen Wujiu placed a lump of soft cloud-clay on the study table. 'A word is not only sound,' he told me. 'It has a *shape* — feel how this one curves.' He pressed my fingers into the clay until I felt the word bend like a living thing under my touch.
shape:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，每个灵咒都有其独特的____，需要用手去感受。
shape:0.hook: When he lifted his hand, the clay held an outline that looked nothing like a word — and everything like a warning.
shape:0.line: 'Every true formula has a *shape* you can hold, not just a sound you can hear.'

twice:0.en: I recited the calming word *twice* before the candle flame steadied. The first time my voice shook and the flame bent wildly; the second time, something inside me settled, and the fire stood straight and tall as a pine. Xiaoxing watched from the doorway, saying nothing.
twice:0.cnHint: 我将那个安神咒____念了____，第二次终于让烛火归于平静。
twice:0.hook: Then Xiaoxing stepped forward and blew the candle out, her eyes unreadable in the sudden dark.
twice:0.line: 'You must say it *twice* — once for the word, once for yourself.'

aspect:0.en: Master Qingwu walked slowly around my practice circle. 'Every formula has more than one *aspect*,' she said, pausing at the eastern corner. 'You have learned its power. You have not yet learned its cost.' The brushwork on the floor glowed faintly, then dimmed.
aspect:0.cnHint: 师尊提醒我，每一门功法都有不止一个____，我只掌握了其中之一。
aspect:0.hook: As she left, the eastern corner of the circle cracked — a clean, straight line pointing toward the mountain's edge.
aspect:0.line: 'The dangerous *aspect* of this word is the one you feel most comfortable with.'

currently:0.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled a long list on the study table. 'These are the words we are *currently* permitted to use,' he said quietly. 'The higher ones are sealed until after the trial.' I counted the permitted words. There were far fewer than I had hoped.
currently:0.cnHint: 师兄向我展示了我们____被允许使用的灵咒名单，数量远少于预期。
currently:0.hook: At the bottom of the list, one word had been crossed out — in fresh ink.
currently:0.line: 'What we are *currently* allowed to use may not be enough for what is coming.'

decrease:0.en: I noticed that the warm light in the study hall had begun to *decrease* as the night deepened. The spiritual lamps fed on the same cloud-energy that powered our words, and something was drawing that energy away. Xiaoxing pressed her palm to the wall and frowned.
decrease:0.cnHint: 书房中的灵气光芒开始____，小星发现能量正在被某种力量抽走。
decrease:0.hook: Outside the window, the sea of clouds below the mountain had risen three full steps since sunset.
decrease:0.line: 'When you feel your strength *decrease*, do not force the word — release it.'

possibility:0.en: Late in the night I sat with my notebook and considered every *possibility*: perhaps the trial would test memory, or endurance, or speed. But Master Qingwu had said only that it would test what we truly were. That single sentence left no comfortable answer to rest on.
possibility:0.cnHint: 深夜我独自思考考验的每一种____，师尊的那句话让所有推测都站不住脚。
possibility:0.hook: A faint sound rose from the sea of clouds below — steady, rhythmic, and not made by wind.
possibility:0.line: 'The *possibility* that frightens you most is usually the one you need to prepare for.'

crucial:0.en: Shen Wujiu tapped the center of the open page. 'This part is *crucial*,' he said. 'Other lines you can improvise if your memory fails, but not this one. If this phrase breaks, the whole formula collapses.' I read the line five times and then closed my eyes to hold it.
crucial:0.cnHint: 师兄指出功法中有一句____的关键咒语，一旦念错整个法阵就会崩溃。
crucial:0.hook: When I opened my eyes, the ink on that single crucial line had faded to near nothing.
crucial:0.line: 'It is *crucial* that you never pause in the middle of that phrase — not even to breathe.'

enormous:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old pine and quiet power. On the central table lay an *enormous* scroll, wider than my arm-span, covered in golden characters that pulsed like a slow heartbeat. Master Qingwu said nothing. She simply placed one finger on the edge, and every lamp in the room dimmed at once.
enormous:0.cnHint: 内殿中央摆着一卷____的古籍，师尊轻触卷边，室内灯火骤暗。
enormous:0.hook: Outside, the wind stopped — completely, suddenly, without reason.
enormous:0.line: 'This *enormous* scroll has not been opened in three hundred years,' said Master Qingwu.

pet:0.en: Xiaoxing kept a small cloud-fox as a *pet*, a pale creature that slept on her sleeve and sneezed soft sparks. That evening it refused to sleep. It sat upright on the windowsill, ears flat, staring east toward the thunderhead that had not moved in three days.
pet:0.cnHint: 小星养了一只云狐作为____，但那夜小狐突然竖耳凝视东方不动的雷云。
pet:0.hook: The fox let out one low cry, then went utterly silent.
pet:0.line: 'My *pet* has never acted this way before,' Xiaoxing whispered.

restaurant:0.en: Before the sect, I had worked in a small *restaurant* below the clouds, carrying bowls and learning nothing of words. Now I stood in a hall where words were power, and I could still feel the weight of those bowls in my palms — a reminder of how far I had yet to climb.
restaurant:0.cnHint: 入门前，叙述者曾在山下____打杂，此刻站在修炼之殿，深感差距之远。
restaurant:0.hook: Then Shen Wujiu said my old life had already been recorded in the sect's memory stone.
restaurant:0.line: 'You left that *restaurant* the night a word-seed appeared in your soup bowl,' said Shen Wujiu.

driver:0.en: Shen Wujiu called himself the *driver* of our study group — the one who set the pace, chose the texts, and kept us from drifting into lazy silence. Tonight he set a text none of us had requested: the Rite of the Coming Storm, page one.
driver:0.cnHint: 师兄自称修炼小组的____，今夜他却主动取出《来风之仪》第一页。
driver:0.hook: He had chosen that text only once before — the night the last tribulation began.
driver:0.line: 'A good *driver* checks the road before the storm, not after,' said Shen Wujiu.

dream:0.en: I had carried the same *dream* since childhood: to stand above the clouds and speak a word that the sky would answer. Tonight, studying alone in the lamp-lit study room, I finally wrote that word on paper — and the paper rose one inch off the desk before settling back.
dream:0.cnHint: 叙述者自幼怀有一个____，今夜独自苦读时，所写之字竟令纸张微微腾空。
dream:0.hook: The word I had written was already fading, as if the page was trying to forget it.
dream:0.line: 'Every disciple here came on the strength of a *dream* alone,' Master Qingwu said softly.

consumer:0.en: Master Qingwu told us that a weak disciple is only a *consumer* of words — taking their power without giving meaning back. A true cultivator becomes part of the word, she said, until the boundary between speaker and spoken dissolves like mist at noon.
consumer:0.cnHint: 师尊说弱者只是词语的____，真正的修炼者要与词语合而为一。
consumer:0.hook: She then looked at me, and I felt certain she was not speaking of the others.
consumer:0.line: 'Do not remain a *consumer* of power you do not yet understand,' Master Qingwu said.

interesting:0.en: Shen Wujiu called my first attempt at the wind-step formula 'very *interesting*,' which, I quickly learned, meant I had done something unexpected — not wrong, not right, but strange enough that he stopped correcting the others and stood watching me alone.
interesting:0.cnHint: 师兄说叙述者初学御风诀时的表现"很____"，随即停下来只盯着他一人观察。
interesting:0.hook: Later he wrote one word in my notebook and underlined it twice.
interesting:0.line: '*Interesting* — your word-trace moves in a direction we have not recorded before,' said Shen Wujiu.

grade:0.en: The sect ranked every disciple by *grade*: white for new, green for growing, gold for those who could speak a word the mountains would hear. I had received my white token that morning. By evening it had turned faintly, inexplicably green at one corner.
grade:0.cnHint: 门派以____区分弟子，叙述者清晨领到白阶令牌，入夜时一角却悄然泛绿。
grade:0.hook: No white token had ever changed color on the first day — not once in the sect's long history.
grade:0.line: 'Your *grade* token does not decide your ceiling,' Master Qingwu said, glancing at my hand.

rule:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled an ancient scroll across the stone table. 'Every disciple must learn one *rule* before dawn,' she said quietly. 'Words are not tools. They are living things. Treat them with care, or they will refuse you.' I copied the first line and felt the ink grow warm under my fingers.
rule:0.cnHint: 清雾师尊展开古卷，告诫弟子每天黎明前必须牢记一条____。
rule:0.hook: At the scroll's edge, a single character began to fade.
rule:0.line: 'There is one *rule* above all others: never speak a word you do not yet understand.'

plant:0.en: Xiaoxing knelt beside a clay pot near the window, pressing a small *plant* into dark soil. 'This herb holds the word for calm,' she told me. 'Water it with steady breath, not anxious hands.' The leaves were pale silver, and they trembled even though no wind moved through the room.
plant:0.cnHint: 小星师妹在窗边种下一株____，说它承载着'静'字的灵力。
plant:0.hook: By midnight the plant had grown three new leaves, each etched with an unknown character.
plant:0.line: 'This *plant* will only bloom if you speak its name without fear.'

national:0.en: Shen Wujiu spread a wide map across the floor. Each floating mountain was marked with a different colour. 'This is the *national* record of every sect,' he said, 'kept since the first word was ever spoken aloud.' I found the Cloud Sea Sect near the map's centre, smaller than I had imagined.
national:0.cnHint: 沈无咎师兄展示一份记录了所有门派的____地图，我发现云海宗比想象中小得多。
national:0.hook: One mountain on the map had no name, only a red circle drawn around it.
national:0.line: 'The *national* record has never listed a sect that vanished — until last year.'

doctor:0.en: A visiting elder known as the *doctor* of words arrived at our hall just before the lamps were lit. He carried no bag, only a thin book pressed to his chest. 'A wrong word, spoken at the wrong hour, is a wound,' he told us. 'I have spent forty years learning how to close such wounds.'
doctor:0.cnHint: 一位被称为字之____的长老在掌灯时分来访，他说错误的词语如同伤口。
doctor:0.hook: Before leaving, the doctor paused and looked at me alone.
doctor:0.line: 'Even a *doctor* of words cannot heal a disciple who refuses to listen.'

economy:0.en: Master Qingwu set three candles on the table and asked which one I would use to light the room. I chose the largest. She shook her head. '*Economy* of power is the first lesson,' she said. 'A small, steady flame outlasts a bright, wasteful one.' I relit the smallest candle and watched it burn all night.
economy:0.cnHint: 清雾师尊用三支蜡烛教导我，灵力的____才是修行第一课。
economy:0.hook: At dawn the small candle still burned, though no wax remained.
economy:0.line: 'The *economy* of your words decides how long your strength will last.'

global:0.en: Shen Wujiu pointed to the sea of clouds far below our window. 'What happens in the deep mist has a *global* effect on every mountain above,' he said. 'One shift in the cloud current can silence a hundred sect halls at once.' I pressed my hand to the cold glass and felt a faint vibration rise from below.
global:0.cnHint: 沈无咎师兄解释，云雾深处的变化对所有浮山都有____性的影响。
global:0.hook: The vibration grew stronger, then stopped all at once.
global:0.line: 'A *global* silence among the sects has happened only twice in history.'

leader:0.en: The scroll named one disciple from each generation as *leader* of the inner hall. Xiaoxing read the list aloud while I held the lamp. Every name was followed by a single word in red — the word that had defined their path. When we reached the current generation, the space after the title was blank.
leader:0.cnHint: 古卷上记载着每一代内堂____的名字，但本代那一行却是空白的。
leader:0.hook: The red ink on the blank line was still wet.
leader:0.line: 'A *leader* is not chosen — the words choose them, when the time is right.'

scientific:0.en: Master Qingwu placed a glass vessel on the table and dropped three herb-words inside. 'Watch carefully,' she said. 'There is a *scientific* reason each word changes colour when it meets the others.' The first word turned gold, the second turned deep blue, and the third went completely dark. She said nothing more.
scientific:0.cnHint: 清雾师尊用三个草药字进行实验，说明字与字相遇时发生变化有其____上的原因。
scientific:0.hook: The dark word inside the vessel began to move on its own.
scientific:0.line: 'A *scientific* mind and a still heart are not opposites — you will need both.'

evidence:0.en: The inner hall smelled of old wood and dried herbs. Master Qingwu walked slowly between the shelves, touching each jar without a word.
